title: Clean halting run
statement: Let $D$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input and output symbols, and state set $S$. Given an initial state $q\in S$, a finite Boolean input $V$, a Boolean $b$, and a natural number $B$, a clean run means that there is a time $T$ at which the machine has halted, its output is exactly the one-bit list $[b]$, every work-tape cell is blank, and every work-tape head is at position $0$. At every time $t\le T$, the absolute position of each work-tape head is at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: A deterministic machine with a natural number of work tapes
